### Personal Automation and Productivity

   Streamline mundane tasks: Use Claude Code to create scripts that automate repetitive computer actions, such as launching and arranging multiple applications at startup. "I used Claude Code to write a powershell script that does all of this for me on launch so when I sign in everything is in its right place."

"mine is dumb but I had claude write a script that watches a folder for screenshots and automatically renames them with a description based on the content." [...] Install:

results.content:
Adam Frankl, The Developer-Facing Startup. Strategy and philosophy: TAB customer discovery, the Hero/Villain/Wise-Advisor story, the DREAM funnel, differentiation levels, net developer retention.
 Jakub Czakon, markepear.dev. Tactical execution: homepage anatomy, developer psychology, channel playbooks (HN, Reddit, X), README/SEO, "market to developers, sell to decision-makers."

And it was pressure-tested by founders who used it as design partners and made it sharper:

 Lubos, founder of hey/api
 Thibault and Max, cofounders of OpenStatus

Where a framework is theirs, the credit is theirs. Where it holds up in practice, that's the founders who tested it. Where it misses, that's on me.

## When you don't want to do it alone [...] That's the day job, and it comes in two shapes:

 The DevTool GTM Company is mine. It's where I work with founders at exactly your stage: very early, often pre-funding, on the strategy and positioning that gets you off the ground. If this pack is helping, that's the human version of it.
 With QC Growth I work with more established teams: seed through Series A and B, including a16z and Sequoia-backed companies, where we do the whole thing: strategy, execution, GTM engineering, and operations.

Free skills for everyone; a human in your corner when the road gets steep. Either way, you're not doing this alone.

Battle-tested a framework? Found a gap? Open an issue or PR, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

MIT, free to use, fork, and distribute. [...] ### 4 · Keep it going

| Skill | Reach for it when… |
 --- |
| founder-led-content | "Marketing" feels gross, so you do none, while your competitor owns the conversation |
| know-if-its-working | You have dashboards full of vanity metrics and no idea whether GTM is actually working |
| market-scan | A rival just rebranded or a new tool appeared, and your positioning is answering last year's market |

## What's inside each skill

Every `SKILL.md` gives you frameworks with actual thresholds (not principles), decision trees for the calls that stall technical founders, the mistakes that look reasonable but quietly kill you, real examples, and a checklist you can run in the next 30 minutes. Written in a founder's language, direct, specific, allergic to fluff.

When Shane O'Connor cooks, if you're a founder or a side project warrior trying to make it out the trenches, you have to be first in line. 🔥
Technical founders struggling with GTM is as old as the internet. Products getting more technical and buyer/user behaviour getting more complex today doesn't help. Shane's made GTMcofounder so going from product to market won't try to break your resolve, like last night 😃
You know it's the good stuff when the onboarding flow is a conversation not a "give me your website url and I'll max print slop content for you".
It's opensource, takes 2-mins of your agent's time to set up while you doomscroll LinkedIn (or your drug of choice), so don't say I didn't do anything good for you 😉
